scope: jarvis_backend/ routers (FastAPI) + credential/secret handling + system host-op boundary; frontend secret-leakage survey

findings.title: system.py host capabilities were unauthenticated
findings.original_state: 11 of 15 routers unauthenticated; system.py host endpoints (processes, files, screenshot, clipboard, launch, provider-settings) had no auth gate.
findings.mitigation: P3/P4: system host-op endpoints now require get_current_user + is_admin (privileged-host). Public surfaces retained only where the frontend depends on them without auth: /status, /dashboard, /capabilities, /launch/apps.

findings.title: Destructive host command lockdown ordering
findings.original_state: POST /system/launch {"app":"shutdown"} returned 401 under an old Depends-before-deny-list ordering (unauth caller got 401 instead of the safety 403).
findings.mitigation: P4: the destructive-command deny-list (_DENY_COMMANDS) is evaluated BEFORE authentication, so shutdown/reboot/halt/poweroff always return 403 even for unauthenticated callers. Legitimate non-destructive launches still work for an authorized admin.
findings.evidence: live probe POST /api/v1/system/launch {"app":"shutdown"} -> 403 'Refusing destructive host command matching shutdown'; test_shutdown_lockdown_unauthenticated; test_shutdown_lockdown_even_when_authenticated
findings.regression_guard: This deny-list-first ordering MUST NOT be reversed.

findings.title: Provider settings exposed raw secret values
findings.original_state: GET /system/provider-settings returned plaintext secret names+values; PUT accepted secret-shaped fields.
findings.mitigation: P6/P7: GET scrubs secret-shaped values to '***' (key names are safe metadata only); PUT rejects any secret-shaped field with HTTP 400 ('Refusing secret-shaped field ...'). Provider credentials are never accepted/edited via the settings API.

findings.title: Three inconsistent secret-handling schemes (Fernet / PBKDF2 / plaintext)
findings.original_state: Legacy plaintext provider secrets persisted in misc.provider_settings; Fernet used by OAuth connectors; PBKDF2 used for password/API-key hashing.
findings.mitigation: P6: canonical credential abstraction established — Fernet (prefix 'fernet:') for encrypted provider secrets via connectors.crypto.encrypt_secret; PBKDF2 (pbkdf2_sha256$...) for password/API-key hashing preserved. Legacy plaintext auto-migrated to Fernet at startup via _migrate_legacy_provider_secrets() (idempotent, keyed off JARVIS_SECRET_KEY). No plaintext provider secrets are accepted by the provider-settings API.

findings.title: Authorization boundary was inconsistent across routers
findings.original_state: Some routers used get_current_user, others had ad-hoc auth; no centralized admin predicate.
findings.mitigation: P3: core.is_admin(user) and core.is_developer(user) are the single authorization predicates (role-name OR is_admin flag OR roles-store wildcard for owner). core._require_admin now delegates to is_admin. system.py reuses these.

findings.title: No defensive security headers
findings.mitigation: P9: SecurityHeadersMiddleware adds nosniff/DENY/no-referrer/Camera+Microphone+Geolocation denial/no-store on every response. CORS origins are validated at import; production mode with default localhost origins raises RuntimeError (fail-closed).

findings.title: Error responses could leak internals
findings.original_state: Unhandled exceptions in system host-op handlers could surface stack traces / absolute file paths.
findings.mitigation: P10: sensitive handlers catch exceptions, log full trace via logger.exception (server-side only), and return generic 'Request failed' / 'File not found' / 403 confinement messages. No traceback or absolute host path is returned to clients.

findings.title: Path traversal on file APIs
findings.mitigation: P4: _confined_path confines reads/lists to ROOT; traversal attempts return 403 'Path is outside the allowed root'.

findings.title: Sensitive host operations were not audited
findings.original_state: No durable audit trail for destructive/permissioned host operations.
findings.mitigation: P8: _audit_system_launch records every launch attempt (denied/executed/error) and _audit_system_action records sensitive system actions, both to audit_logs, with the authenticated actor (or 'anonymous' for pre-auth deny-list hits).

findings.title: Frontend models a provider-secret settings flow
findings.original_state: frontend/web/src/lib/api.ts declares a ProviderSettings interface (secret-shaped field names) and an updateProviderSettings PUT path.
findings.mitigation: P7/P11 boundary: the backend PUT rejects secret-shaped fields (400) and GET scrubs values to '***', so raw provider secrets can never reach the model/AI layer or be returned to the frontend. The frontend contains NO hardcoded secret values (scan-verified; only empty-string defaults and field-name types). Residual: the settings input form is backend-blocked but not yet removed from the UI (low-priority debt).
findings.evidence: P14 source scan (no sk-/AKIA/BEARER literals in frontend or backend production code); test_get_scrubs_secret_values; test_put_rejects_secret_shaped_fields

findings.title: Knowledge dashboard crashes on undefined category (user-reported)
findings.original_state: getCategoryColor(category) called category.toLowerCase() on an undefined category -> TypeError.
findings.mitigation: getCategoryColor now accepts category?: string|null and guards with (category || '').toLowerCase(); KnowledgeCard renders a fallback color.

findings.title: Out-of-scope unauthenticated routers (future SEC-2)
findings.original_state: ai, billing, global_knowledge, knowledge, memory, multimodal, media, voice, codegen, monitoring, stark, misc remain unauthenticated (not in SEC-1 Phase-4 system.py scope).
findings.mitigation: Not expanded in SEC-1 (out of scope; 'do not redesign / add unrelated features'). Documented for follow-up.

findings.title: gateway.py imports a non-existent vault module (latent import)
findings.original_state: jarvis_backend/gateway.py imports infrastructure/vault/manager which is not on disk; ai.py imports gateway lazily and main.py does not import chat_service/gateway at startup, so no startup ImportError occurs.
findings.mitigation: No blocking runtime impact (lazy import). Documented as latent; do not eager-import gateway at startup.
findings.evidence: backend start log 'JARVIS backend started. ai_enabled=False'; python -c 'import jarvis_backend.main' builds app ok

secret_store_registry.name: PBKDF2 password/API-key hashing
secret_store_registry.caller: auth.py login/register, API-key creation/rotation (auth.py api_keys), user seeding (core.start_backend)
secret_store_registry.rotation: re-hash on password change / API-key rotation

secret_store_registry.name: Fernet encrypted provider secrets
secret_store_registry.algorithm: Fernet (PBKDF2-derived key off JARVIS_SECRET_KEY via crypto._fernet)
secret_store_registry.rotation: re-encrypt on key rotation (keyed off JARVIS_SECRET_KEY)
secret_store_registry.migration: plaintext provider secrets auto-migrated to Fernet at startup (idempotent)

secret_store_registry.name: JWT access / refresh tokens
secret_store_registry.location: in-memory refresh_tokens store + issued to client
secret_store_registry.algorithm: HS256 (JARVIS_SECRET_KEY), short-lived access; refresh token hashed at rest
secret_store_registry.encryption_state: access token in transit (client), refresh token hashed at rest

secret_store_registry.name: OAuth connector secrets (per-provider)
secret_store_registry.encryption_state: ciphertext; NEVER returned to API consumers
